title: ROM-safe reproducible baseline
summary: Established the reproducible, redistributable baseline: a ROM-free CIA and 3DSX, deterministic corresponding source, private SD packaging, and automated emulator/network verification.
highlights: Native Emerald execution through the pinned gpSP 3DS core.
ROM validation and ignored private SD-card packaging.
Online presence, chat, emotes, reconnect, and original project branding.
verification: 16 protocol, runtime, and web tests passed.
Azahar headless boot, reconnect, keepalive, movement, chat, and emote smoke passed.
Release audit confirmed no ROM, save, identity, configuration, or avatar atlas in public artifacts.
knownIssues: Historical build; use the current release for testing.
Physical May/two-client coverage and final display-orientation acceptance were still open.
upgradeNotes: Preserve the private ROM, save, avatar atlas, and configuration files.
Install the current CIA through FBI; copying a CIA alone does not update an installed title.

Public release/help/status boards and paired beta, defect, code, feature, multiplayer, and general boards.
Moderation reports, sanctions, audit history, soft deletion, search, subscriptions, and rate limits.
verification: 25 normal tests and both PostgreSQL lifecycle tests passed.
A live synthetic identity paired, posted privately, stayed anonymous publicly, and was completely deleted.
Production WSS enrollment passed in Azahar.
knownIssues: Physical Old 3DS WSS and browser-pairing acceptance remained pending.
This build is superseded; do not use it for new testing.

Paired profiles, integrity-labelled leaderboards, anomaly review, and complete stats deletion.
Readable E71 stage, TLS result, certificate flags, clock skew, and log-path diagnostics.

title: Experimental link transport
summary: Introduced the opt-in, two-player Serial-Poke feasibility transport with bounded relay rooms and automatic rotating save backups. It remains transport evidence, not a claim that battles or trades are ready.
highlights: Strictly opt-in link_room configuration and two-authenticated-player room limit.
Save backup must be flushed and fsynced before gpSP link mode starts.
Newest-three backup retention and hard-disconnect recovery testing.
verification: Two isolated Azahar profiles passed startup and hard-interruption cycles.
Production WSS relayed 53 bounded synthetic packets and recovered after a guest disconnect.
Measured average round trip was 171 ms with 4.5 ms mean absolute jitter.
knownIssues: No Cable Club packet was observed from the available title-screen state.
Battles, trades, save integrity under interruption, and physical performance remain unaccepted.
Public battle/trade invitations and rankings remain disabled.
upgradeNotes: Use a fresh unpredictable room code and independent save backups for any link experiment.
Do not continue unless both clients show ACTIVE - BACKUP OK.

title: Service observability and capacity guardrails
summary: Adds privacy-safe production telemetry, a maintained Grafana dashboard, and deliberately bounded concurrent load testing while leaving the game protocol and private player data unchanged.
highlights: Cluster-internal Prometheus metrics for aggregate players, rooms, protocol activity, capacity, database readiness, memory, and uptime.
A 12-panel Emerald Online 3DS Grafana dashboard for service health and experimental-link visibility.
A safety-bounded load harness that defaults to loopback and refuses remote targets without explicit operator opt-in.
verification: All 50 automated tests passed against disposable PostgreSQL 17 with zero skips.
A 32-client, five-second local run delivered 768 state updates and 24,080 snapshots with 32 of 32 pongs and zero protocol errors, rejections, or authentication failures.
The release audit verified the public source archive excludes Markdown, operational infrastructure, private addresses, credentials, ROMs, saves, and branded assets.
knownIssues: Experimental Cable Club battles and trades still require progressed private save state and physical-hardware acceptance before Gate 5 can begin.
FPS can fluctuate by device and cutscene; toggling Online off and back on after the scene remains the documented workaround.
upgradeNotes: Existing 0.8.0 clients remain protocol-compatible; this release primarily improves server operations and release evidence.
If updating the console build, preserve emerald.gba, saves, identity.cfg, stats.cfg, and avatars.t3x.

title: Gate 4 emulator stability and verified save handoff
summary: Stabilizes the Azahar interpreter and nonblocking network paths used by physical-to-emulator Cable Club testing, and validates progressed Emerald saves before creating a private test bundle.
highlights: Interpreter mode no longer touches unmapped 3DS dynarec caches, preventing the Azahar preflight crash.
Nonblocking peer polling now supplies the socket metadata Azahar requires while remaining compatible with physical ctrulib networking.
Gate 4 bundles require checksum-valid Emerald save slots and record only non-identifying progress facts; ROMs, saves, identities, and preferences remain private.
verification: All 53 automated tests passed against disposable PostgreSQL 16 with zero skips.
Azahar 2126.0 loaded the checksum-valid progressed save, authenticated through production WSS, entered the isolated link room, and remained alive beyond the former crash point.
Normal local-TCP and production-WSS Azahar smokes passed; all synthetic production identities were deleted afterward.
knownIssues: A real physical-to-Azahar Cable Club battle, trade, interruption, save comparison, audio check, and Old 3DS performance check are still required before Gate 5.
Azahar intentionally uses the slower gpSP interpreter because its 3DS emulation does not provide the physical console's Luma dynarec bootstrap.
Remote trainer overlays can remain visible during battles because stale map coordinates were treated as overworld state; fixed in 0.8.3.
upgradeNotes: Preserve emerald.gba, emerald.sav, identity.cfg, stats.cfg, avatars.t3x, and any link-backups before copying the new 3DSX or reinstalling the CIA.
Merely copying the CIA to /cias/ does not update the installed HOME Menu title; select it in FBI and choose Install and delete CIA.

highlights: Requires the exact supported Emerald US CB2_Overworld callback before accepting map coordinates.
Checks Emerald's in-battle flag as a second independent guard.
Revalidates the game context at draw time so stale presence cannot cross a scene transition.
verification: Runtime regression coverage asserts the supported gMain layout, Thumb callback address, battle flag, presence gate, and draw-time gate.
The complete automated suite passes after the hotfix.

Map Chat shows sender, server UTC timestamp, and message in a scrollable current-map session list, with a separate Compose control.
Save-derived statistics are cached for one second instead of rescanning Pokédex flags every frame, reducing unnecessary Old 3DS CPU work while preserving upload freshness.
verification: Protocol coverage proves the global roster spans different maps while ordinary snapshots remain same-map only.
A maximum 16-user roster page remains below the 4096-byte protocol limit, and chat delivery includes a validated ISO 8601 timestamp.

title: RFU Union Room trade verified in Azahar
summary: Moves the private Gate 4 link experiment to gpSP's Emerald RFU backend, services packets inside its tight response window, and completes a native two-Azahar Union Room trade through save and restart while leaving normal presence, chat, and offline play unchanged.
highlights: Uses gpSP's Emerald RFU backend for opt-in link rooms; testers must use Emerald's RFU/Union Room route rather than the unsupported Direct Corner path.
Drains nonblocking link packets from gpSP's receive callback and polls once per emulated frame during an active link session instead of waiting for the normal 100 ms presence interval.
Preserves Emerald's temporary RFU host scan cycles while clearing explicit peer withdrawal or disconnect state, preventing discovery from being broken by a routine HOST_STOP.
Suppresses online presence overlays on Emerald's native multiplayer maps and requests the New 3DS CPU/L2 speedup where supported.
verification: Automated source coverage checks RFU selection, per-frame linked polling, callback receive draining, New 3DS speedup, native-multiplayer overlay suppression, and scan-safe peer cleanup.

Two isolated Azahar 2126.0 clients discovered native avatars and a Trading Board offer, exchanged Torchic for Marill, completed Emerald's automatic save, restarted, and reloaded parties containing two Marill on CODEX and two Torchic on LINZ.
The ROM-free CIA and 3DSX were rebuilt with the version 0.8.7 stamp, and the corresponding-source archive contains the exact runtime and modified gpSP source.
The release checksum manifest covers all three current public artifacts and the privacy-focused release audit validates the source archive and forum catalogs.

Public link invitations and battle/trade rankings remain disabled.
